 Tinglayan gets P20M for disaster recovery;‘Funds will go where they are intended’- Mayor Abay
 Mark Moises Calayan 15 hours ago 2 min read TABUK CITY, Kalinga  – The Municipality of Tinglayan has been allocated P20 million in national government assistance to support its disaster recovery efforts, including the rehabilitation of communities and infrastructure damaged by Super Typhoon Uwan in November 2025. 
 Mayor Charles Abay welcomed the funding, describing it as a major help to the people of Tinglayan and assuring that the amount would be used for its intended purpose. 
 "Dakkel nga tulong dayta iti umili ti Tinglayan. We thank the national government, the president and Governor James Edduba for the good news," Abay said in a phone interview on November 16. 
 The assistance is intended to help the municipality restore damaged infrastructure and other essential services affected by natural disasters. 
 Governor James S. Edduba announced the allocation during the Kapehan meeting at the Provincial Capitol on November 16, following the ceremonial turnover of Disaster Rehabilitation and Recovery Assistance Program (DRRAP) funds led by President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. at Malacañang on November 5. 
 Tinglayan was among the municipalities in Kalinga that suffered widespread damage during Super Typhoon Uwan in November 2025. 
 At the height of the typhoon, the municipality was placed under Signal No. 4. Clearing operations continued even after the storm had passed, as soil, rocks, and fallen trees blocked road sections leading to remote barangays. 
 The storm also damaged homes and agricultural areas. The Provincial Government of Kalinga’s consolidated situation report dated November 24, 2025, recorded 3,124 families affected by the typhoon in Tinglayan. 
 The P20-million allocation is expected to help address rehabilitation and recovery needs identified by the local government. 
 Aside from Tinglayan, Edduba announced DRRAP allocations of P20 million for Tabuk City, P15 million for Lubuagan, P10 million for Pasil, and P5 million for Rizal. 
 The provincial government also received P50 million in assistance. 
 Edduba said President Marcos had issued strict instructions to ensure that DRRAP funds would not be misused or spent on ghost and substandard projects. 
 “Very strict ang instruction ni President, no ghost project, no substandard project at walang gagalansya dito because this is DRRM funds, that’s why it’s directly downloaded to the local government,” Edduba said during the MANCOM meeting.
